objective: To generate employment opportunities in rural and urban areas through the establishment of new self-employment ventures and micro-enterprises.
benefits: Margin money subsidy support under PMEGP along with bank-linked financing for eligible new micro-enterprises.
target_beneficiary: Individuals above 18 years of age seeking to establish eligible new micro-enterprises, including applicants from special categories where applicable.
eligibility_rules: Applicant must be above 18 years of age.
There is no income ceiling for setting up a new PMEGP project.
For manufacturing projects costing above Rs. 10 lakh, the applicant must have passed at least Class VIII.
For business or service projects costing above Rs. 5 lakh, the applicant must have passed at least Class VIII.
Assistance is available only for eligible new projects sanctioned under PMEGP.
Existing units that have already received Government subsidy under another Central or State Government scheme are generally not eligible for assistance for a new PMEGP unit.
Only one person from one family can normally receive financial assistance for setting up a new enterprise under PMEGP.
required_documents: Aadhaar card
Passport-size photographs
Project report
Educational qualification certificate, where applicable
Caste certificate, where applicable
Special category certificate, where applicable
Rural area certificate, where applicable
EDP or skill-development training certificate, where applicable
Other supporting documents required under the applicable PMEGP eligibility criteria

objective: To provide access to institutional collateral-free credit for micro enterprises engaged in income-generating activities.
benefits: Collateral-free credit under four categories: Shishu up to Rs. 50,000, Kishore above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh, Tarun above Rs. 5 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakh, and Tarun Plus above Rs. 10 lakh and up to Rs. 20 lakh for eligible entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid a previous Tarun loan.
target_beneficiary: Micro enterprises and entrepreneurs engaged in income-generating manufacturing, trading and service activities, including eligible activities allied to agriculture.
eligibility_rules: The loan must be for an eligible income-generating micro-enterprise activity.
Eligible activities include manufacturing, trading and services, as well as specified activities allied to agriculture.
Both term-loan and working-capital requirements can be financed under PMMY.
Shishu covers loans up to Rs. 50,000.
Kishore covers loans above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh.
Tarun covers loans above Rs. 5 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakh.
Tarun Plus covers loans above Rs. 10 lakh and up to Rs. 20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid a previous Tarun-category loan.
Final loan sanction remains subject to the lending institution's appraisal and applicable lending requirements.
required_documents: Identity and address proof as required by the lending institution
Business or activity details
Bank account and financial details as required by the lender
Quotation or details of machinery, equipment or proposed expenditure, where applicable
Business registration or supporting business documents, where applicable
Documents required by the selected bank, NBFC or MFI for credit appraisal

objective: To provide end-to-end holistic support to traditional artisans and craftspeople working with their hands and tools, including recognition, skill development, modern tools, credit support, digital incentives and market linkages.
benefits: Recognition through PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card, skill training with stipend, toolkit incentive of Rs. 15,000, collateral-free enterprise development loans of Rs. 1 lakh and Rs. 2 lakh in two tranches at a concessional beneficiary interest rate of 5%, digital transaction incentives and marketing support.
target_beneficiary: Traditional artisans and craftspeople working on a self-employment basis in one of the 18 family-based traditional trades covered under PM Vishwakarma.
eligibility_rules: Applicant must be an artisan or craftsperson working with hands and tools and engaged in one of the 18 traditional trades covered under PM Vishwakarma.
Applicant must be at least 18 years old on the date of registration.
Applicant must be engaged in the concerned traditional trade on the date of registration.

Applicant should not have availed a loan under similar Central or State Government credit-based self-employment or business-development schemes such as PMEGP, PM SVANidhi or Mudra during the previous 5 years, subject to official scheme conditions.
Registration and benefits are restricted to one member of a family.
For this scheme, family generally consists of husband, wife and unmarried children.
A person in Government service and their family members are not eligible under the scheme.
required_documents: Aadhaar card
Bank passbook / bank account proof
Ration card
Aadhaar details of all family members if the beneficiary does not have a ration card
Additional Supporting Documents

objective: To facilitate bank loans to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs for setting up greenfield enterprises.
benefits: The original Stand-Up India scheme provided composite bank loans from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore for eligible greenfield enterprises. The Department of Financial Services states that this scheme was operational up to 31 March 2025.
target_beneficiary: Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs establishing eligible greenfield enterprises.
eligibility_rules: The original scheme was intended for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs above 18 years of age.
The enterprise was required to be a greenfield project in an eligible sector.
For a non-individual enterprise, at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake was required to be held by an eligible Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe or woman entrepreneur.
The borrower was required not to be in default to any bank or financial institution.
The Department of Financial Services states that Stand-Up India was operational up to 31 March 2025.
This record must not be treated as an indication that new Stand-Up India applications are currently open.

scheme_name: Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)
objective: To organize traditional industries and artisans into clusters, improve production and value addition, enhance skills and marketability, and strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of traditional industry clusters.
benefits: Cluster-based assistance covering activities such as skill development, capacity building, improved tools and production processes, common facilities, product development, packaging, marketing and other approved interventions under SFURTI.
target_beneficiary: Traditional industry clusters and artisans supported through eligible implementing and nodal agencies under the SFURTI framework.
eligibility_rules: SFURTI is primarily a cluster-development scheme rather than a normal direct individual business loan scheme.
Proposals are implemented through the institutional structure specified in the SFURTI guidelines, including eligible Nodal Agencies and Implementing Agencies.
The proposed cluster must relate to eligible traditional industries and artisan communities.
Assistance and approval are subject to the current SFURTI guidelines and evaluation of the cluster proposal.
An individual artisan should not be shown a direct personal loan application flow merely because this scheme appears in semantic search results.
required_documents: Detailed Project Report for the proposed cluster
Cluster and artisan details required under SFURTI
Implementing Agency information and supporting records
Technical and financial proposal information
Land or infrastructure-related documents where applicable
Other documents required by the SFURTI portal and applicable guidelines

objective: To promote first entrepreneurial projects of first-generation entrepreneurs in Tamil Nadu through entrepreneurship support, bank-linked finance, capital subsidy and interest subvention.
benefits: For eligible manufacturing or service projects costing from Rs. 10 lakh up to Rs. 5 crore, the scheme provides 25% individual-based capital subsidy subject to a maximum of Rs. 75 lakh and 3% interest subvention throughout the repayment period.
target_beneficiary: Eligible first-generation entrepreneurs in Tamil Nadu establishing manufacturing or service enterprises.
eligibility_rules: Applicant must be a first-generation entrepreneur.
General-category applicants must normally be between 21 and 45 years of age.
For specified special categories including Women, BC, MBC, SC, ST, Ex-servicemen, Transgenders and Differently Abled persons, the upper age limit is relaxed up to 55 years.
Applicant must possess an eligible educational qualification such as Higher Secondary, Degree, Diploma, ITI or Vocational Training.
The project must be an eligible manufacturing or service project.
Eligible project cost ranges from Rs. 10 lakh up to Rs. 5 crore.
Promoter contribution is 10% for General category and 5% for eligible Special category applicants.
Loan assistance is provided through eligible financial institutions including TIIC, Commercial Banks and TAICO Banks.
required_documents: Proof of age such as Transfer Certificate or school/college record
Ration Card or applicable nativity/address proof
Aadhaar card or voter identity proof where applicable
Degree, Diploma, ITI or other applicable educational qualification certificate
Community certificate where applicable
Special-category certificate where applicable
Project report
Rental, lease agreement or ownership document where applicable
Machinery or equipment quotations with applicable GST details
Partnership deed where applicable
Land and building-related documents where applicable

scheme_name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
objective: To strengthen credit delivery to Micro and Small Enterprises by providing guarantee cover for eligible credit facilities extended by Member Lending Institutions.
benefits: CGTMSE provides guarantee cover to eligible credit facilities extended by Member Lending Institutions. Under the current Credit Guarantee Scheme-I framework, eligible credit facilities can be covered up to Rs. 10 crore per eligible borrower for specified lending institutions, subject to scheme conditions and applicable guarantee coverage percentages.
target_beneficiary: Eligible Micro and Small Enterprises receiving qualifying credit facilities from CGTMSE Member Lending Institutions.
eligibility_rules: CGTMSE is a credit-guarantee mechanism and is not itself a direct business loan or grant to an entrepreneur.
The underlying credit facility must be extended by an eligible Member Lending Institution.
The borrower must be an eligible Micro or Small Enterprise under the applicable CGTMSE scheme.
Fund-based and/or non-fund-based eligible credit facilities may be covered subject to applicable scheme conditions.
For specified banks and financial institutions, guarantee coverage can apply to eligible credit facilities up to Rs. 10 crore per eligible borrower.
Guarantee coverage percentages depend on borrower category, enterprise category and other applicable CGTMSE conditions.
The lending institution performs the credit appraisal and applies for CGTMSE guarantee coverage.
required_documents: There is no single direct entrepreneur-to-CGTMSE application document checklist because guarantee coverage is processed through the Member Lending Institution.
Business and KYC documents required by the lending institution
Loan application and project or business information required by the lending institution
Financial statements or financial information where applicable
Udyam or enterprise-related records where required by the lender
Other documentation required by the Member Lending Institution for credit appraisal and CGTMSE coverage

scheme_name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME)
objective: To support the formalisation, upgradation and competitiveness of micro food-processing enterprises and strengthen food-processing value chains.
benefits: Eligible individual micro food-processing enterprises can receive credit-linked capital subsidy at 35% of eligible project cost, subject to a maximum subsidy of Rs. 10 lakh per unit. Beneficiary contribution must be at least 10% of project cost, with the balance generally financed through bank credit.
target_beneficiary: Eligible existing or new micro food-processing enterprises, individual entrepreneurs and other eligible entities covered under PMFME guidelines.
eligibility_rules: The enterprise must undertake an eligible micro food-processing activity under PMFME.

Support is available for eligible expansion or upgradation of existing micro food-processing enterprises and for setting up eligible new micro food-processing enterprises under the applicable guidelines.

Enterprises involved in the district's One District One Product product may receive preference, while other eligible micro food-processing enterprises may also be considered subject to scheme guidelines.
Individual units may receive credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost up to a maximum of Rs. 10 lakh per unit.
Beneficiary contribution must be at least 10% of project cost.
The remaining funding requirement is generally met through bank finance.
Activities specifically excluded under the applicable PMFME guidelines are not eligible.
required_documents: Identity and KYC documents
Business or enterprise details
Project report or Detailed Project Report as applicable
Bank and financing information
Machinery or equipment quotations where applicable
Business registration or enterprise records where applicable
Land, building, lease or ownership records where applicable
Other documents required by the PMFME application process, State Nodal Agency or lending bank

objective: To provide medium-to-long-term debt financing support for investment in eligible post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
benefits: Eligible loans under the financing facility receive interest subvention of 3% per annum on an amount up to Rs. 2 crore per project for a maximum period of 7 years, subject to applicable AIF guidelines.
target_beneficiary: Eligible farmers, agri-entrepreneurs, Farmer Producer Organisations, cooperatives, Self Help Groups, startups and other entities covered under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund guidelines.
eligibility_rules: The applicant must belong to an eligible beneficiary category under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund.
The project must involve an eligible infrastructure or asset under the applicable AIF guidelines.
Eligible loans receive 3% annual interest subvention on an amount up to Rs. 2 crore per project.
Interest subvention is available for a maximum period of 7 years.
For loans exceeding Rs. 2 crore, interest subvention is limited to the eligible amount up to Rs. 2 crore.
Loan sanction remains subject to appraisal by the participating lending institution.
Other project, location and beneficiary conditions specified in current AIF guidelines must be satisfied.
required_documents: Applicant KYC and identity documents
Project report or Detailed Project Report
Business or entity registration documents where applicable
Land ownership, lease or project-site documents where applicable
Project cost and financing details
Machinery, equipment or infrastructure quotations where applicable
Bank and financial documents required by the lending institution
Other documents required by the AIF portal or participating lender

objective: To mitigate unemployment among socially and economically weaker sections in Tamil Nadu by supporting eligible unemployed persons to establish self-employment business enterprises.
benefits: For eligible trading or business projects, project cost can be up to Rs. 15 lakh. Individual-based capital subsidy is 25% of project cost subject to a maximum of Rs. 3.75 lakh. Promoter contribution is 10% for General category and 5% for eligible Special category applicants.
target_beneficiary: Eligible unemployed persons in Tamil Nadu seeking to establish new trading or business enterprises.
eligibility_rules: Applicant must be at least 18 years of age.
The current Tamil Nadu MSME scheme page states an upper age limit of 45 years for General category applicants and relaxation up to 55 years for specified Special category applicants.
Applicant must have passed at least Class VIII.
Family annual income must be below Rs. 8 lakh according to the current Tamil Nadu MSME scheme description.
The current scheme description covers eligible trading or business projects with project cost up to Rs. 15 lakh.
Promoter contribution is 10% for General category and 5% for eligible Special category applicants.
The scheme provides individual-based capital subsidy of 25% of project cost subject to a maximum of Rs. 3.75 lakh.
Loan assistance is provided through eligible commercial banks.
Applicants should rely on the current portal and latest Government Orders where older FAQ documents contain superseded limits.
required_documents: Proof of age
Educational qualification certificate
Aadhaar or applicable identity proof
Address or residence proof
Family income certificate or applicable income proof
Community certificate where applicable
Special-category certificate where applicable
Project report
Business-related quotations where applicable
Bank and other supporting documents requested in the online application
